Fractions are a way of expressing parts of a whole, represent numbers between two whole numbers or a ratio between two quantities. They consist of two numbers separated by a horizontal or slanted line, with the number above the line called the numerator and the number below the line called the denominator.

On the basis of Numerator and Denominator, fractions are of two types. That is,

  • Proper Fraction
  • Improper Fraction

Improper Fractions

An improper fraction is one in which the numerator is higher than or greater than the denominator, such as 7/3 and 12/5. They always represent a value higher than 1.

Every Improper Fraction is a Rational Number but vice-versa is not always true.

Example: We have Fraction 5/4 its a improper fraction as here numerator is greater than denominator. After dividing 5 by 4 , the result will be 1.25 which is a terminating after decimal , therefore its an rational number.

Difference Between Proper and Improper Fraction

Some of the key difference between proper and improper fractions are:

FeatureProper FractionImproper Fraction
DefinitionNumerator is less than the denominator.Numerator is greater than or equal to the denominator.
ValueAlways less than 1.Equal to or greater than 1.
RepresentationCan be a part of a whole.Can represent a whole number or more.

Example

Examples of proper fractions are 7/13, 4/5, 1/2, 2/7, etc.

Examples of improper fractions are 15/13, 14/5, 11/2, 12/7, etc.

How to Convert Improper Fractions to Mixed Fraction?

Improper fractions and mixed fractions are the two ways of representing the same number and so they are equivalent. To change improper fraction to mixed fraction use the steps discussed below,

Step 1: As we know that in improper fractions the numerator is always greater than the denominator. Divide the numerator by the denominator value.
Step 2: In the division process obtain the quotient and remainder.
Step 3: Arrange all the values obtained in Step 2 as,

Fraction in Mixed Form = Quotient(Remainder/Denominator)

The same can be understood by studying the example added below:

Convert 17/4 into a mixed fraction.

We have 17/4
Dividing the fraction we get,
17 = 4 × 4 + 1

  • Quotient = 4
  • Remainder = 1

In Mixed Fraction Form,
= 4(1/4)
This is the required mixed fraction form.

Convert Mixed Fraction to Improper Fraction

We know that any improper fraction can be easily written as mixed fractions or mixed number. A mixed fraction is a type of fraction that is written in the form of a(b/c) and is read as "a whole b by c". Some examples of mixed fractions are 4(2/3), 6(3/5), etc.

We can easily change mixed fractions into improper fractions by following the method.

Suppose we have to find the improper fraction of mixed fraction a(b/c) then the steps to follow are,

Step 1: Multiply the denominator(c) of the mixed fraction with the whole number(a) i.e. a×c
Step 2: Add the value of the numerator with the multiple obtained in Step 1 as, (a×c) + b
Step 3: Simplify (a×c) + b and write it as a numerator where the denominator is c the fraction so obtained is the required fraction.

Study the example given below for better understanding.

Change 11(3/5) into an improper fraction.

Given, 11(3/5)

the numerator for the improper fraction is equal to the sum of the current numerator and the product of denominator and the whole part
( 11×5) + 3 = 58

the improper fraction for 11(3/5)
11(3/5) = 58/5.

Solved Examples on Improper Fractions

Example 1. Identify the improper fractions: 11/5, 27/15, 3/12, 11/13, 15/7, 61/6

Solution: 

11/5, 27/15, 15/7 and 61/6 are improper fractions as the value of the numerator is greater than the value of the denominator for these fractions.

Example 2. Write 22/8 as mixed fraction.

Solution: 

Converting 22/8 into an improper fraction,

22= (2 × 8)+6 

thus, 22/8 = 2\frac{6}{8}

Example 3. Write 1\frac{5}{6} as an improper fraction.

Solution: 

Given fraction : 1\frac{5}{6}
to obtain the numerator of the improper fraction we multiply the denominator with the whole part and add the current numerator .

So, (6 × 1) + 5  = 11
the new numerator will be 11 and the denominator will remain same.

1\frac{5}{6} as an improper fraction is equal to 11/6.
